```{python}
import yaml

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("../..").resolve()))
```

## Background




The original master equation in the Simpson's contagion paper assumes that the infection rate follows a powerlaw kernel that is the probability that is in a group(fully connected clique) of $n$ agents $i$ of which are infected the transmission rate is 

$$\beta(i | \lambda, \nu)=\lambda \nu^\alpha$$

Where $\lambda$ controls the base rate of infection and $\nu$ controls the non-linearity. When $nu = 1$ the kernel is linear.

We write down a Approximate master equation(AME) to track the evolution of the system. We track the evolution *within* each group excactly and approximate the between group infecetions with a moment closure $\rho(t)$. Which averages transmission probabilities over all groups. 

We see that $\hat{beta}(n,i,t) = \frac{\int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty \lambda i^\nu G_i^{(n,\lambda,\nu)}(t) d\lambda d\nu}{\int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty G_i^{(n,\lambda,\nu)}(t) d\lambda d\nu}$


We can then tract the *kernel variation* as 

$$\delta \tilde{\beta}(t) = \frac{\tilde{\beta}(t) - \tilde{\beta}(t-1)}{\tilde{\beta}(t)}$$

There is also a second version of the kernel variation, a stranger and rarer type of variation. 


$$ \Delta \tilde{\beta}(n,i) = \frac{\int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty i^\nu - (i-1)^{\nu} h_i^{n,\lambda,\nu}d\lambda d\nu}{\int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty h_i^{n,\lambda,\nu} d\lambda d\nu}$$



So $\delta \tilde{\beta}$ tracks the kernel variation averaged over all groups at time t. Wheras $\Delta \tilde{\beta}$ tracks the kernel variation *within* each group, averaged over all groups. This helps control for the selection bias 






```{python}
def delta_beta(c):
    """Compute increments δβ(ν) = c(ν) - c(ν-1), with c(0)=0 implied."""
    c = np.asarray(c)
    return np.diff(np.concatenate([[0], c]))


def load_sweep(config_path, sweep_name):
    """Load all completed kernel_mode_summary files, tagged with their parameters."""
    with open(config_path) as f:
        config = yaml.safe_load(f)
    instances = build_synthetic_instances(config)

    rows = []
    for inst in instances:
        data_name = inst["data_name"]
        p = RESULTS / sweep_name / "synthetic" / data_name / INST_DIR / "kernel_mode_summary.parquet"
        if not p.exists():
            continue
        df = pd.read_parquet(p)
        df = df[df["source_param"] == "mu"].copy()
        # flatten overrides into columns
        ov = inst["overrides"]
        df["epsilon"]   = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("epsilon", float("nan"))
        df["data_name"] = data_name
        rows.append((ov, df))
    return instances, rows


def power_law_kernel(lam, alpha, nu_max):
    nu = np.arange(1, nu_max + 1, dtype=float)
    return nu, np.clip(lam * nu**alpha, 0, 1)


def fit_log_slope(nu, vals):
    """Fit log(mu) ~ b*log(nu) and return b (apparent exponent)."""
    mask = (nu > 0) & (vals > 0)
    if mask.sum() < 3:
        return float("nan")
    b = np.polyfit(np.log(nu[mask]), np.log(vals[mask]), 1)[0]
    return b
```

## Mechanism A — Degree heterogeneity (same kernel, unequal blocks)

```{python}
with open("../../configs/simpson_mech_a_20260508.yaml") as f:
    cfg_a = yaml.safe_load(f)

_, rows_a = load_sweep("../../configs/simpson_mech_a_20260508.yaml", "simpson_mech_a_20260508")

# Decode phi and alpha from overrides
records_a = []
for ov, df in rows_a:
    phi   = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("phi", 0.5)
    eps   = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("epsilon", float("nan"))
    kerns = ov.get("contagion", {}).get("kernels", [{}])
    alpha = kerns[0].get("alpha", float("nan"))
    lam   = kerns[0].get("lam", float("nan"))
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        records_a.append(dict(phi=phi, epsilon=eps, alpha=alpha, lam=lam,
                              nu=row["nu"], median=row["median"],
                              ci_low=row["ci_low"], ci_high=row["ci_high"]))

df_a = pd.DataFrame(records_a)
print(f"Completed: {df_a['data_name'].nunique() if 'data_name' in df_a.columns else len(rows_a)}/{64} datasets")
print(f"Parameter grid: alpha={sorted(df_a.alpha.unique())}, phi={sorted(df_a.phi.unique())}, epsilon={sorted(df_a.epsilon.unique())}")
```

### Inferred vs. true kernel — ε=0.9 (highest assortativity)

Each panel: posterior median (solid) ± 90% CI vs. true power-law kernel (dashed black).

```{python}
eps_show = 0.9
alphas = sorted(df_a.alpha.unique())
phis   = sorted(df_a.phi.unique())
NU_MAX = 20

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(alphas), len(phis), figsize=(14, 10), sharey="row", sharex=True)
cmap = plt.get_cmap("Blues")
phi_colors = {phi: cmap(0.35 + 0.55 * i / max(1, len(phis)-1)) for i, phi in enumerate(phis)}

for ri, alpha in enumerate(alphas):
    for ci, phi in enumerate(phis):
        ax = axes[ri, ci]
        sub = df_a[(df_a.alpha == alpha) & (df_a.phi == phi) & (df_a.epsilon == eps_show)]

        # true kernel
        nu_t, k_t = power_law_kernel(0.15, alpha, NU_MAX)
        ax.plot(nu_t, k_t, "k--", lw=1.8, alpha=0.7, label="True" if ci == 0 else None, zorder=4)

        if len(sub) > 0:
            sub = sub.sort_values("nu")
            nu_inf = sub["nu"].values
            ax.plot(nu_inf, sub["median"].values, color=phi_colors[phi], lw=2, zorder=3,
                    label=f"Inferred" if ci == 0 else None)
            ax.fill_between(nu_inf, sub["ci_low"].values, sub["ci_high"].values,
                            color=phi_colors[phi], alpha=0.18)

            # compute and annotate apparent exponent
            b_inferred = fit_log_slope(nu_inf, sub["median"].values)
            ax.annotate(f"b̂={b_inferred:.2f}", xy=(0.97, 0.07), xycoords="axes fraction",
                        ha="right", fontsize=8, color=phi_colors[phi])
        else:
            ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "pending", transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=9, color="gray")

        ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.5, ls=":")
        ax.set_xlim(0.5, NU_MAX + 0.5)
        ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.15, ls=":")
        ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
        ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
        if ri == 0:
            ax.set_title(f"φ={phi}", fontsize=10)
        if ci == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel(f"α={alpha}\np(infect|ν)", fontsize=9)
        if ri == len(alphas) - 1:
            ax.set_xlabel("ν (infected neighbours)", fontsize=9)

fig.suptitle(
    f"Mechanism A — inferred vs. true kernel (ε={eps_show})\n"
    "b̂ = apparent log-log exponent of inferred kernel (true α ≤ 1)",
    fontsize=12, y=1.01,
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### δβ(ν) — incremental infection rate, ε=0.9

The Simpson signature: each block's true δβ is **declining** (sublinear kernel), but the K=1 inferred δβ may be **rising** (apparent complex contagion).

```{python}
# Pick one representative φ per panel to avoid clutter (largest imbalance)
phi_show = max(phis)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(alphas), figsize=(14, 4), sharey=False)

for ci, alpha in enumerate(alphas):
    ax = axes[ci]
    sub = df_a[(df_a.alpha == alpha) & (df_a.phi == phi_show) & (df_a.epsilon == eps_show)]

    # true δβ
    nu_t, k_t = power_law_kernel(0.15, alpha, NU_MAX)
    db_true = delta_beta(k_t)
    ax.plot(np.arange(1, NU_MAX + 1), db_true, "k--", lw=2, label="True δβ", zorder=4)

    if len(sub) > 0:
        sub = sub.sort_values("nu")
        db_inf  = delta_beta(sub["median"].values)
        db_low  = delta_beta(sub["ci_low"].values)
        db_high = delta_beta(sub["ci_high"].values)
        nu_inf  = sub["nu"].values
        ax.plot(nu_inf, db_inf, color=phi_colors[phi_show], lw=2, label="Inferred δβ", zorder=3)
        ax.fill_between(nu_inf, db_low, db_high, color=phi_colors[phi_show], alpha=0.18)

    ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.5, ls=":")
    ax.set_title(f"α={alpha}", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("ν", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlim(0.5, NU_MAX + 0.5)
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.15, ls=":")
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    if ci == 0:
        ax.set_ylabel("δβ(ν) = c(ν) − c(ν−1)", fontsize=10)
        ax.legend(fontsize=9)

fig.suptitle(
    f"Mechanism A — δβ increments (ε={eps_show}, φ={phi_show})\n"
    "Declining true δβ + rising inferred δβ = Simpson's contagion",
    fontsize=11, y=1.02,
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Apparent exponent vs. true α — all ε

```{python}
# Compute apparent exponent for every completed run
exponent_rows = []
for ov, df in rows_a:
    phi   = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("phi", 0.5)
    eps   = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("epsilon", float("nan"))
    kerns = ov.get("contagion", {}).get("kernels", [{}])
    alpha = kerns[0].get("alpha", float("nan"))
    sub = df[df["source_param"] == "mu"].sort_values("nu")
    b = fit_log_slope(sub["nu"].values.astype(float), sub["median"].values)
    exponent_rows.append(dict(phi=phi, epsilon=eps, alpha=alpha, apparent_exponent=b))

exp_df_a = pd.DataFrame(exponent_rows)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(alphas), figsize=(13, 4), sharey=True)
eps_vals = sorted(exp_df_a.epsilon.unique())
eps_colors = {e: plt.cm.plasma(i / max(1, len(eps_vals)-1)) for i, e in enumerate(eps_vals)}

for ci, alpha in enumerate(alphas):
    ax = axes[ci]
    sub = exp_df_a[exp_df_a.alpha == alpha]

    for phi in sorted(sub.phi.unique()):
        psub = sub[sub.phi == phi].sort_values("epsilon")
        ax.plot(psub.epsilon, psub.apparent_exponent,
                marker="o", ms=6, lw=1.5, label=f"φ={phi}", alpha=0.85)

    ax.axhline(alpha, color="black", lw=1.5, ls="--", alpha=0.7, label=f"True α={alpha}")
    ax.axhline(1.0,   color="gray",  lw=1.0, ls=":",  alpha=0.5, label="Linear (b=1)")
    ax.set_xlabel("ε (assortativity)", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_title(f"True α={alpha}", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2, ls=":")
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    if ci == 0:
        ax.set_ylabel("Apparent log-log exponent b̂", fontsize=10)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)

fig.suptitle(
    "Mechanism A — apparent exponent b̂ vs. ε, coloured by φ\n"
    "b̂ > true α means Simpson inflation; b̂ > 1 means apparent complex contagion",
    fontsize=11, y=1.02,
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Paper-style figure: δβ̃ vs. Δβ̃ cloud plot (Mechanism A)

For Mechanism A, the intrinsic kernel is exactly the same for all nodes, meaning $\delta\beta_{dense}(\nu) = \delta\beta_{sparse}(\nu) = \delta\beta_{true}(\nu)$. Because of this, the composition-weighted average $\Delta \tilde{\beta}(\nu)$ perfectly overlaps the true $\delta\beta(\nu)$. The paradox occurs entirely because the inferred $\delta\tilde{\beta}$ pulls away from $\Delta \tilde{\beta}$ due to the structural coarse-graining of the network topologies.


## Results 

In this test we construct a stochastic block model 

```{python}
_, rows_b = load_sweep("../../configs/simpson_mech_b_20260508.yaml", "simpson_mech_b_20260508")

records_b = []
for ov, df in rows_b:
    eps    = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("epsilon", float("nan"))
    omega  = ov.get("contagion", {}).get("assignment", {}).get("omega", 0.0)
    kerns  = ov.get("contagion", {}).get("kernels", [{}, {}])
    alpha  = kerns[0].get("alpha", float("nan"))
    lam_hi = kerns[0].get("lam", float("nan"))
    lam_lo = kerns[1].get("lam", float("nan")) if len(kerns) > 1 else float("nan")
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        records_b.append(dict(epsilon=eps, omega=omega, alpha=alpha,
                              lam_hi=lam_hi, lam_lo=lam_lo,
                              contrast=round(lam_hi / lam_lo, 2) if lam_lo > 0 else float("nan"),
                              nu=row["nu"], median=row["median"],
                              ci_low=row["ci_low"], ci_high=row["ci_high"]))

df_b = pd.DataFrame(records_b)
n_done = len(rows_b)
print(f"Completed: {n_done}/192 datasets")
if n_done > 0:
    print(f"alpha={sorted(df_b.alpha.unique())}")
    print(f"lam_lo={sorted(df_b.lam_lo.unique())}")
    print(f"epsilon={sorted(df_b.epsilon.unique())}")
    print(f"omega={sorted(df_b.omega.unique())}")
```

### Inferred vs. true kernel — ε=0.9, ω=0.0

```{python}
eps_show, omega_show = 0.9, 0.0
lam_los = sorted(df_b.lam_lo.unique()) if len(df_b) > 0 else []

if len(df_b) == 0 or len(lam_los) == 0:
    print("Mechanism B results still pending — check back once sweep completes.")
else:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(alphas), len(lam_los), figsize=(14, 10), sharey="row", sharex=True)
    cmap_b = plt.get_cmap("Oranges")
    lo_colors = {l: cmap_b(0.35 + 0.55 * i / max(1, len(lam_los)-1)) for i, l in enumerate(lam_los)}

    for ri, alpha in enumerate(alphas):
        for ci, lam_lo in enumerate(lam_los):
            ax = axes[ri, ci]
            sub = df_b[
                (df_b.alpha == alpha) & (df_b.lam_lo == lam_lo) &
                (df_b.epsilon == eps_show) & (df_b.omega == omega_show)
            ]

            # true kernel for HIGH block (what each block actually uses)
            nu_t, k_hi = power_law_kernel(0.3, alpha, NU_MAX)
            nu_t, k_lo = power_law_kernel(lam_lo, alpha, NU_MAX)
            ax.plot(nu_t, k_hi, "k--", lw=1.5, alpha=0.6,
                    label="True hi" if ci == 0 else None, zorder=4)
            ax.plot(nu_t, k_lo, color="gray", lw=1.5, ls=":", alpha=0.6,
                    label="True lo" if ci == 0 else None, zorder=4)

            if len(sub) > 0:
                sub = sub.sort_values("nu")
                ax.plot(sub["nu"], sub["median"], color=lo_colors[lam_lo], lw=2, zorder=3,
                        label="Inferred" if ci == 0 else None)
                ax.fill_between(sub["nu"], sub["ci_low"], sub["ci_high"],
                                color=lo_colors[lam_lo], alpha=0.18)
                b = fit_log_slope(sub["nu"].values.astype(float), sub["median"].values)
                ax.annotate(f"b̂={b:.2f}", xy=(0.97, 0.07), xycoords="axes fraction",
                            ha="right", fontsize=8, color=lo_colors[lam_lo])
            else:
                ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "pending", transform=ax.transAxes,
                        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9, color="gray")

            ax.set_xlim(0.5, NU_MAX + 0.5)
            ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
            ax.grid(True, alpha=0.15, ls=":")
            ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
            ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
            if ri == 0:
                ax.set_title(f"λ_lo={lam_lo}\n(ratio={0.3/lam_lo:.1f}×)", fontsize=9)
            if ci == 0:
                ax.set_ylabel(f"α={alpha}\np(infect|ν)", fontsize=9)
            if ri == len(alphas) - 1:
                ax.set_xlabel("ν (infected neighbours)", fontsize=9)

    fig.suptitle(
        f"Mechanism B — inferred vs. true kernel (ε={eps_show}, ω={omega_show})\n"
        "Columns: λ_hi/λ_lo contrast ratio. b̂ = apparent exponent of inferred kernel.",
        fontsize=12, y=1.01,
    )
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

## Paper-style figure: δβ̃ vs. Δβ̃ cloud plot (Mechanism B)

```{python}
DATA = Path("../..") / "data" / "processed" / "synthetic"

def load_instance_data(data_name, sweep_name):
    M   = pd.read_parquet(DATA / data_name / "M.parquet").values
    N   = pd.read_parquet(DATA / data_name / "N.parquet").values
    kms = pd.read_parquet(
        RESULTS / sweep_name / "synthetic" / data_name / INST_DIR / "kernel_mode_summary.parquet"
    )
    kms = kms[kms["source_param"] == "mu"].sort_values("nu").reset_index(drop=True)
    return M, N, kms


def make_paper_panel(ax, data_name, sweep_name, alpha, lam_hi, lam_lo,
                     phi=0.5, n_nodes=512, nu_max=25):
    split = int(n_nodes * phi)   # nodes 0..split-1 → k_hi,  split..n-1 → k_lo
    M, N, kms = load_instance_data(data_name, sweep_name)

    nu_arr    = np.arange(1, nu_max + 1, dtype=float)
    prev_arr  = np.concatenate([[0.0], nu_arr[:-1]])           # [0,1,2,...,nu_max-1]
    db_hi_arr = lam_hi * (nu_arr**alpha - prev_arr**alpha)     # declining for alpha<1
    db_lo_arr = lam_lo * (nu_arr**alpha - prev_arr**alpha)

    # ── Gray cloud: per-node TRUE kernel variation, sized by event count ──
    # db_true[node, nu_idx] = λ_block · (ν^α − (ν−1)^α)  for ν = nu_idx+1
    is_hi    = np.arange(n_nodes) < split
    db_true  = np.where(is_hi[:, None], db_hi_arr[None, :], db_lo_arr[None, :])  # (n, nu_max)
    total    = (M[:, 1:nu_max+1] + N[:, 1:nu_max+1]).astype(float)               # (n, nu_max)
    valid    = total > 0
    ni, vi   = np.where(valid)
    ax.scatter(vi + 1, db_true[ni, vi],
               s=np.sqrt(total[ni, vi]) * 10,
               color="gray", alpha=0.06, linewidths=0, zorder=1)

    # ── Δβ̃: event-weighted average of per-block true δβ ─────────────────
    total_hi  = (M[:split,  1:nu_max+1] + N[:split,  1:nu_max+1]).sum(axis=0)
    total_lo  = (M[split:,  1:nu_max+1] + N[split:,  1:nu_max+1]).sum(axis=0)
    total_all = total_hi + total_lo
    Delta_beta = np.where(
        total_all > 0,
        (total_hi * db_hi_arr + total_lo * db_lo_arr) / total_all,
        np.nan,
    )
    ax.plot(nu_arr, Delta_beta, color="black", lw=2, ls="--",
            marker="x", ms=5, markevery=2, zorder=4, label=r"$\Delta\tilde{\beta}(n,\nu)$")

    # ── True per-block δβ (colored dashed, both declining) ───────────────
    ax.plot(nu_arr, db_hi_arr, color="#1565c0", lw=1.8, ls="--", alpha=0.85, zorder=3,
            label=f"True δβ hi  λ={lam_hi}")
    ax.plot(nu_arr, db_lo_arr, color="#e65100", lw=1.8, ls="--", alpha=0.85, zorder=3,
            label=f"True δβ lo  λ={lam_lo}")

    # ── δβ̃: inferred K=1 kernel variation (black solid + circles) ────────
    nu_inf    = kms["nu"].values.astype(float)
    med       = kms["median"].values
    lo_ci     = kms["ci_low"].values
    hi_ci     = kms["ci_high"].values
    db_inf    = np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.0], med]))
    db_inf_lo = np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.0], lo_ci]))
    db_inf_hi = np.diff(np.concatenate([[0.0], hi_ci]))
    mask = nu_inf <= nu_max
    ax.plot(nu_inf[mask], db_inf[mask], color="black", lw=2.5,
            marker="o", ms=4.5, zorder=5, label=r"$\delta\tilde{\beta}(n,\nu)$")
    ax.fill_between(nu_inf[mask], db_inf_lo[mask], db_inf_hi[mask],
                    color="black", alpha=0.10, zorder=2)

    ax.set_xlim(0.5, nu_max + 0.5)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.4, ls=":")
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.12, ls=":")
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
```

```{python}
# Illustrative single panel: α=0.7, λ_lo=0.05 (strongest contrast), ε=0.9
with open("../../configs/simpson_mech_b_20260508.yaml") as f:
    cfg_b_raw = yaml.safe_load(f)
insts_b_all = build_synthetic_instances(cfg_b_raw)

b_lookup = {}
for inst in insts_b_all:
    ov     = inst["overrides"]
    eps    = ov.get("graph", {}).get("params", {}).get("epsilon")
    omega  = ov.get("contagion", {}).get("assignment", {}).get("omega", 0.0)
    kerns  = ov.get("contagion", {}).get("kernels", [])
    a      = kerns[0].get("alpha") if kerns else None
    ll     = kerns[1].get("lam")   if len(kerns) > 1 else None
    if eps == 0.9 and omega == 0.0:
        b_lookup[(a, ll)] = inst["data_name"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
make_paper_panel(ax, b_lookup[(0.7, 0.05)], "simpson_mech_b_20260508",
                 alpha=0.7, lam_hi=0.3, lam_lo=0.05, nu_max=25)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of infectious neighbours  ν", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Contagion rate variation  δβ", fontsize=12)
ax.legend(fontsize=9, loc="upper right")
ax.set_title(
    r"Simpson's contagion — Mechanism B  (α=0.7, λ_hi=0.3, λ_lo=0.05, ε=0.9)"
    "\nGray cloud: per-node true δβ sized by event count"
    r"  |  Cloud shifts up as ν grows  →  apparent $\delta\tilde{\beta}$ rises",
    fontsize=9,
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# Full 4×4 grid
alphas_p  = sorted({k[0] for k in b_lookup})
lam_los_p = sorted({k[1] for k in b_lookup})
LAM_HI    = 0.3

nrows, ncols = len(alphas_p), len(lam_los_p)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols,
                         figsize=(4.5 * ncols, 3.8 * nrows),
                         sharey=False, sharex=True)

for ri, alpha in enumerate(alphas_p):
    for ci, lam_lo in enumerate(lam_los_p):
        ax  = axes[ri, ci]
        dn  = b_lookup.get((alpha, lam_lo))
        kms_path = (RESULTS / "simpson_mech_b_20260508" / "synthetic"
                    / dn / INST_DIR / "kernel_mode_summary.parquet")
        if dn is None or not kms_path.exists():
            ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "no data", transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center")
            continue
        make_paper_panel(ax, dn, "simpson_mech_b_20260508",
                         alpha=alpha, lam_hi=LAM_HI, lam_lo=lam_lo, nu_max=25)
        if ri == 0:
            ax.set_title(f"λ_lo={lam_lo}  ({LAM_HI/lam_lo:.0f}× contrast)", fontsize=10)
        if ci == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel(f"α={alpha}\nδβ", fontsize=9)
            if ri == 0:
                ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right")
        if ri == nrows - 1:
            ax.set_xlabel("ν (infected neighbours)", fontsize=9)

fig.suptitle(
    r"Mechanism B — $\delta\tilde{\beta}$ vs $\Delta\tilde{\beta}$ grid  (ε=0.9, ω=0, λ_hi=0.3)"
    "\nGray cloud: per-node true δβ  |  Black solid: inferred δβ̃  |  Black dashed: Δβ̃  |  Colored: per-block true δβ",
    fontsize=10, y=1.01,
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
